nodes.description: External function disperseTokenSimple that loops over 3 recipients and pulls tokens from msg.sender via token.transferFrom.
Caller-controlled address used as the 'from' argument of token.transferFrom, determining whose tokens are moved.
External call to an arbitrary, attacker-supplied IERC20 token contract whose boolean return is enforced by require; target address and behavior are not trusted.
Unchecked uint256 multiplication of a caller-supplied value by 10**18 under Solidity 0.6.x, which can silently overflow.
IERC20 token address supplied by the caller; fully controllable external contract.
Fixed-size address[3] array of transfer destinations supplied by the caller.
Fixed-size uint256[3] array of amounts supplied by the caller and scaled by 10**18.
Loop counter iterating over the recipients/values arrays.

edges.reason: The function body invokes the external token.transferFrom call inside a loop, exposing control to an untrusted token contract that may reenter.
Execution reaches the unchecked values[i]*10**18 multiplication, which can overflow uint256.
msg.sender flows directly into the from parameter of token.transferFrom, so the caller selects the source of the pulled tokens.
The caller-supplied token parameter is the target contract of the external transferFrom call.
Elements of the caller-supplied recipients array flow into the to parameter of token.transferFrom.
Caller-supplied values array elements flow into the unchecked multiplication values[i]*10**18.
The local loop counter i governs loop iteration and therefore controls how many times the function body executes.

normalization_plan.reason: The token parameter exists only to supply the target contract for the external transferFrom call.
The recipients array parameter only supplies the destination addresses of token.transferFrom.
The values array parameter is consumed exclusively by the unchecked scaling multiplication before being passed to transferFrom.
The local loop counter has no independent semantics and only drives the enclosing function's loop.
